close-reopen-revival.text: What ships, and the accepted design

What ships today is ckeri close by the current keys, documented on Close your identity checkpoint. The accepted design (D-036 to D-040) is the reap by the next keys and the revival through the registry. Play Alice leaves and Alice comes back through the registry and the registry simulation. There is no withdraw. Conviction is the only terminal state.

Alice leaves. That is the reap, the only close there is, and not a current-key close: a witnessed rotation by the next keys whose signed message names the payee of the premium (the fee for landing a rotation) and the refund address. The premium goes to that payee when the pool of advance funds covers it; otherwise the payee is paid nothing — an unpaid close is still a close. Everything else goes to the refund address; the token burns; the registry leaf is parked — no checkpoint on chain — holding the hash of that key state.

A relayer with the public rotation cannot reap: the payee and the address are one message the new keys sign. Mallory holding only the stolen current keys cannot reap. Mallory holding the next keys can: that is control (pre-rotation).
Parked is not gone. Nothing on chain but the leaf. Top-up, poison (the owner's own lock), freeze, rotate, register-again are all refused. Two ways out:

Revival. A witnessed rotation later than the parked key state, with fresh bonds, a first pool, a refund address chosen by whoever pays, born juvenile (younger than the window W a consumer waits out). Replaying the close's own rotation is refused.
Conviction. A duplicity proof against the parked key state. Terminal. No value flows: there is no UTxO to seize.
Coming back, the checkpoint is consumable only after the juvenility window W. Registering the same AID again is refused forever: the token is minted once.
The close page is the V1 command that ships on preprod. Do not read it as the accepted design.
